title: What If the Ogallala Aquifer Ran Dry?

scenes.text: What if the water under America's breadbasket ran out? Farmers are already pumping it faster than it refills.
The Ogallala Aquifer sits under eight states and covers about 174,000 square miles.
It supplies about 30 percent of the groundwater used for irrigation across the whole United States.
Pumping since 1950 has cut its stored water by about 9 percent, and in parts of Texas it refills roughly 0.024 inches a year.
A 2013 study projected that nearly 70 percent of the groundwater in parts of it could be used up by about 2060.
Once it's empty, natural refilling could take hundreds to thousands of years. We're spending in decades what took ages to store.
